title: Core ideas in mathematics
description: The ideas the rest of mathematics rests on, from proof and primes to calculus.

ideas.title: Proof
ideas.summary: A proof shows that a statement must be true, by steps of logic from things already accepted.

items.q: In mathematics, what is an axiom?
items.a: A statement accepted without proof and used as a starting point

items.q: In mathematics, what is a conjecture?
items.a: A statement believed to be true but not yet proved

items.q: Which method of proof assumes the opposite of a claim and shows that this leads to an impossibility?
Which method of proof shows a statement holds for 1, and then that if it holds for n it also holds for n + 1?

ideas.title: Prime numbers
ideas.summary: Every whole number above 1 is a product of primes in exactly one way, and the primes never run out.

items.q: What is a prime number?
items.a: A whole number greater than 1 whose only divisors are 1 and itself

items.q: What does the fundamental theorem of arithmetic say?
items.a: Every whole number above 1 is a product of primes in exactly one way, apart from order

items.q: Which ancient Greek mathematician gave the classic proof that there are infinitely many prime numbers?
What is the prime factorization of 60?

ideas.title: Functions
ideas.summary: A function is a rule that gives exactly one output for each input.

items.q: In mathematics, what is a function?
items.a: A rule that assigns exactly one output to each input

items.q: What is the set of all allowed inputs of a mathematical function called?
What is the slope of the line y = 3x + 2?

ideas.title: Exponentials and logarithms
ideas.summary: Exponential growth multiplies by a fixed factor in each equal step, and the logarithm undoes it.

items.q: What kind of growth multiplies a quantity by the same factor in each equal step of time?
What is the logarithm base 10 of 1000?
What is the approximate value of e, the base of the natural logarithm?
Which rule rewrites the logarithm of a product, log(ab), as a sum?

ideas.title: The derivative and the integral
ideas.summary: The derivative measures a rate of change, the integral adds up a total, and each undoes the other.

items.q: In calculus, what does the derivative of a function measure?
items.a: Its instantaneous rate of change: the slope of its graph at a point

items.q: What is the derivative of x^2 with respect to x?
In calculus, what does the definite integral of a positive function between two points give, as a picture?
items.a: The area under its graph between those two points

items.q: What does the fundamental theorem of calculus say about differentiation and integration?
items.a: They are inverse operations: each undoes the other

items.q: Which two people developed calculus independently in the late 1600s?
items.a: Isaac Newton and Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz

ideas.title: Circles and triangles
ideas.summary: A few exact relations between lengths, angles and areas hold for every triangle and every circle.

items.q: What does the Pythagorean theorem say about a right triangle with legs a and b and hypotenuse c?
What ratio defines the number pi?
items.a: A circle's circumference divided by its diameter, about 3.14159

items.q: What is the formula for the area of a circle of radius r?
What do the interior angles of a triangle on a flat plane add up to?
